decision: persist worker-side pending mutation request IDs and reconcile them through authenticated request-status after restart
selected: atomic local pending-request state + coordinator status reconciliation

alternatives.name: atomic local pending-request state + status reconciliation
alternatives.notes: Preserves the exact requestId before send, survives worker restart, composes with the existing transactional coordinator, and leaves unknown outcomes pending instead of guessing.

alternatives.name: blind retry with a fresh requestId
alternatives.notes: Fast but can duplicate a committed mutation after response loss and defeats coordinator idempotency.

alternatives.name: memory-only pending request map
alternatives.notes: Simple but loses the request identity on the exact worker restart case this task must close.

alternatives.name: coordinator-issued request IDs
alternatives.notes: Can be strong but needs an extra round trip or session protocol before every mutation and expands the transport/state machine.

winnerReason: The selected approach closes the worker-restart ambiguity gap with the smallest protocol change. It records mutation identity durably before transport, reuses the same identity on retry, and reconciles terminal outcomes after restart without re-running the mutation.
failuresAndLessons: A response can be lost after coordinator commit; transport failure is not proof that the mutation failed.
A durable coordinator journal is insufficient if the worker forgets the requestId after restart.
Unknown or non-terminal status must remain pending; recovery must never invent success or failure.
Crash after a successful response but before local clear is safe because restart reconciliation observes the coordinator's terminal record and then clears the local pending entry.
scope: synthetic orchestration and defensive lab reliability only; no real financial transactions or external side effects
